settingsHandler manages the disk-writable representation of winapp2ool module properties for persistence between sessions by deserializing the winapp2ool.ini file into their respective module settings, monitoring any changes during the session and serializing them back to disk as needed.

A parallel settings backend powered by iniFile2.
SettingsFile2 is the single authoritative in-memory representation for modules that have been migrated away from the legacy settingsDict + settingsFile dual-representation.
During the transition period, settingsHandler keeps SettingsFile2 up to date via Load2 (called from loadSettings) and SetValue2 (called from updateSettings). Migrated modules call LoadModule2 / SaveModule2 instead of the legacy LoadModuleSettingsFromDict / createModuleSettingsSection.

member.summary:
UWPBuilder is a winapp2ool module which handles the generation of winapp2.ini entries for Universal Windows Platform applications installed under %LocalAppData%\Packages .

It reads from a single source directory containing:
UWP.ini
The scaffold template with one or more [EntryScaffold: ...] sections. Each scaffold's DetectFileBase= lines are expanded per package to produce the entry's detection paths, and its FileKeyBase= lines are applied to every application as a consistent baseline set of cleaning targets.

member.name: T:winapp2ool.Diff
member.summary:
Compares two winapp2.ini format iniFile s and summarizes the changes to the user
NOTE: to "exist" here means for an entry of the same exact name (case sensitive) to exist
Changes fall three major categories:
Added entries exist in the new file and not in the old file
Modified entries exist in both the new file and the old file and have been changed in some way
Removed entries exist in the old file but not in the new file
Additionally, Removed entries have three sub categories:
Renamed entries do not exist in the new file, but their content exists in some other entry in the file, mostly unchanged from the old version (may contain minor changes)
Merged entries do not exist in the new file, but their content exists in some other entry in the new file which is substantially different from the old version
Removed without replacement do not exist in the new file and their content was not found in some other entry in the new file
Likewise, Merged entries themselves are broken into two categories
Modified Entries that existed in the old file which have been modified to contain content from entries which have been removed
Added Entries which did not exist in the old file but who contain content from entries which have been removed

member.name: T:winapp2ool.Transmute
member.summary:
Transmute (formerly Merge ) is a winapp2ool module which provides the ability to modify an iniFile2 object using the contents of a separate iniFile2 object with conflict resolution at different levels of granularity.
In the parlance of Transmute, there are two files of interest:
The 'base' file and the 'source' file
The 'base' file is the one whose content will be modified by the operation. That is, this file will be either added to, removed from, or have some or all of its content modified
Likewise, the 'source' file is the one from which the modifications will be provided. That is, this file will have its content added to, removed from, or replace content in the 'base' file
Transmute modes:
Add (Default transmute mode)
Adds sections to the base file from the source file
If a section from the source file exists in the base file, the individual keys will be added
Replace
Replace has two sub modes: BySection and ByKey
ByKey (Default replace mode): Replaces the value of keys in the base file with values from the source file based on their Name
BySection: Replaces entire sections in the base file with the section of the same name in the source file.
Note: Replace does nothing with sections from the source file not found in the base file
Remove
Remove has two sub modes: BySection and ByKey
ByKey (Default remove mode): Removes keys from individual sections within the base file
Keys must be provided within a section in the source file and will be removed from the corresponding section of the same name in the base file
Remove Key Modes:
ByName : Removes keys based on matching key names only
Removing a key with this mode requires knowledge of its Name. This works best for unnumbered keys (in the context of winapp2.ini, keys like Section, or unnumbered Detection keys) but also works for numbered keys if you know the number. For numbered keys it is generally best to try using the ByValue remove mode
ByValue : Removes keys based on matching key values. The KeyType (key name without numbers) must also match. Works best for numbered keys whose numbers may change or be unclear when invoking Transmute
Additionally, Transmute provides an important function called Flavorize. Flavorize is used to apply "flavors" to an ini file. In the context on winapp2.ini, there has historically existed at least one flavor: the "non-ccleaner" file. Flavorize automates and also democratizes what has historically been a very labor intensive process: Maintaining a concise set of transformations on the base winapp2.ini that can be used to adapt it to different purposes. The flavorization process always takes in a base ini file and then applies operations in the following order:
Section Removal -> Key Name Removal -> Key Value Removal -> Section Replacement -> Key Replacement -> Section and Key Additions
member.remarks:
Remarks:
Transmute replaces the Merge module and has has three modes which are wholly discrete from one another. This is a breaking change from old versions of Merge prior to 2025, which always add entries which don't exist and perform conflict resolution as part of that process.
As the functionality of Merge evolved, it no longer felt appropriate to refer to its output as the result of a "merger" necessarily. We now consider the resulting output a Transmutation. Nevertheless, this is still spiritually the Merge module

member.summary:
BrowserBuilder is a winapp2ool module which handles the generation of bespoke winapp2.ini entries for a very large number of web browsers. It provides a small scripting interface which allows for the dynamic creation of entire groups of winapp2.ini entries using a limited set of easily accessed information.
All input files are read from a single configurable source directory. At minimum, that directory must contain at least one of chromium.ini or gecko.ini - the specially formatted ruleset files that drive entry generation. BrowserBuilder is primarily intended as a small devops tool but end users might find it useful as it enables them to generate entries for non-standard installation paths or portable applications while keeping winapp2.ini up to date separately
Additionally, and because it is intended to simplify the devops, Browser Builder expects to "Flavorize" the browsers.ini that it produces. This is done so as to resolve over and under coverages by generated entries as well as resolve incompatibilities. Accordingly, it expects but does not require a set of Flavor correction files in the source directory (up to 1 "Add" file, up to 3 "Remove" files, and up to 2 "Replace" files) - all resolved by canonical name. Consult the Transmute documentation for more information about Flavors

member.name: T:winapp2ool.Trim
member.summary:
Trim is a winapp2ool module that evaluates the detection criteria of each entry in a winapp2.ini file against the current machine and removes any entries whose detection criteria are not satisfied, producing a system-specific subset of the full database.
The full winapp2.ini database contains entries for thousands of applications, the vast majority of which will not be installed on any given machine. Trimming eliminates those irrelevant entries, reducing load time for cleaning software (particularly CCleaner) and avoiding spurious scans.
Detection criteria and evaluation order:
DetectOS
Evaluated first. If present and not satisfied by the current Windows version, the entry is immediately discarded without checking any other criteria.
If satisfied and no other detection keys are present, the entry is retained.
DetectOS values take the form VERSION| (minimum), |VERSION (maximum), or VERSION1|VERSION2 (range), where version numbers are major.minor doubles (e.g. 6.1 for Windows 7, 10.0 for Windows 10).
Detect
Registry paths checked for existence. If any Detect key matches a registry key present on the current system, the entry is retained.
DetectFile
Filesystem paths (supporting wildcards) checked for existence. If any DetectFile key matches a file or directory present on the current system, the entry is retained.
SpecialDetect
Deprecated CCleaner variable checked against a hardcoded list of well-known browser/application install locations. Supported values: DET_CHROME , DET_MOZILLA , DET_THUNDERBIRD , DET_OPERA . If the corresponding application is detected, the entry is retained. Parsing for this is left only to support very old versions of winapp2.ini.
Entries with no detection keys of any kind are always retained.
Include and exclude overrides:
When enabled, the includes file ( TrimFile2 ) and excludes file ( TrimFile4 ) each contain a list of entry names (one per ini section header) that unconditionally override the normal detection evaluation. An entry whose name appears in the includes file is always retained regardless of whether its detection criteria are satisfied. An entry whose name appears in the excludes file is always removed regardless of whether its detection criteria are satisfied. Include and exclude checks run before any detection evaluation.
Environment variable expansion:
In addition to standard Windows environment variables, Trim resolves several CCleaner-specific variables that do not exist natively in the Windows environment:
%Documents% %UserProfile%\My Documents on XP; %UserProfile%\Documents on Vista+
%CommonAppData% %AllUsersProfile%\Application Data on XP; %AllUsersProfile%\ on Vista+
%LocalLowAppData% %UserProfile%\AppData\LocalLow
%Pictures% %UserProfile%\My Documents\My Pictures on XP; %UserProfile%\Pictures on Vista+
%Music% %UserProfile%\My Documents\My Music on XP; %UserProfile%\Music on Vista+
%Video% %UserProfile%\My Documents\My Videos on XP; %UserProfile%\Videos on Vista+
%ProgramFiles% receives special handling: paths under %ProgramFiles% are checked against both the native-bitness Program Files directory and the 32-bit Program Files (x86) directory on 64-bit systems, so entries covering 32-bit applications installed on 64-bit Windows are retained correctly.
VirtualStore augmentation:
For entries that pass detection, Trim inspects the entry's FileKeys, RegKeys, and ExcludeKeys and generates additional keys covering VirtualStore locations that correspond to paths found under %ProgramFiles% , %CommonAppData% , %CommonProgramFiles% , and HKLM\Software . VirtualStore keys are only appended when the corresponding VirtualStore path actually exists on the current system, ensuring the output remains accurate to the machine.
